Cloudflare Sinks 14% and Datadog 13% in a Week as Software Selloff Hits Cloud Stocks ©Iulian Catalin's Images and luthfil aziman effendi from Gambar Luthfil aziman effendi via Canva
Key Takeaways

Cloudflare stock fell 14% in the week to Oct. 30, and Datadog fell 13%, though neither company reported weak results.

ServiceNow's and Fortinet's reports revived fears that AI will disrupt software, and Friday's tech selloff did most of the damage.

Cloudflare's Nov. 5 report has to clear a guide of 31% revenue growth and show gross margin holding near 73%.

The stock is cheaper but still richly valued, and Datadog's Nov. 4 report lands first.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) stock fell 14% in the week to Oct. 30, closing Friday at $280.70, and Datadog (DDOG:NASDAQ) fell 13% to $235.27. Neither company reported weak results. Both got caught in a software selloff that peaked on Friday.

Software's bad week

ServiceNow and Fortinet reported after the close on Oct. 28. The next day, Fortinet fell about 20% after cutting its full-year service revenue forecast, and ServiceNow fell 27%, its worst day on record. That revived the fear that AI is disrupting software.

Then on Friday, Oct. 30, weak results from Amazon and Intel deepened doubts about whether AI spending will pay off. The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5%, Datadog lost 11.5%, and Cloudflare lost 9.5%.

Cloudflare had started the week right after a 7% jump on Oct. 23, as the PHP flaws lifted security stocks. CEO Matthew Prince said exploit attempts on Cloudflare's network climbed from thousands before the flaws were disclosed to millions after.

The one company-specific item was a disclosure, not a result. On Oct. 26, Cloudflare reported that a bug in one Workers AI model sent 155 responses containing other customers' data between Aug. 27 and Sept. 9. The company says it fixed the issue on Sept. 9 and found no evidence of deliberate exploitation.

Datadog is in the same boat

Datadog also had no news of its own. Its second-quarter revenue grew 36% to $1.12 billion, but its third-quarter guide of $1.135 billion to $1.145 billion implies roughly 29% growth from a year earlier. It reports before the open on Nov. 4, a day ahead of Cloudflare, so a clean beat there would ease some of the pressure on its neighbor.

The bar for Nov. 5

For the third quarter, Cloudflare guided to $736 million to $737 million of revenue (31% growth) and $0.34 of adjusted EPS. Analysts expect revenue to more than double from 2025 to 2028:

Cloudflare (NET): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)

Nothing in the selloff gives them a reason to cut those numbers.

Gross margin is the weak spot. Cloudflare's GAAP gross margin fell to 74.5% in fiscal 2025 from 77.3% a year earlier, a decline management has tied to carrying more traffic:

What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after underwhelming earnings reports from tech giants Amazon and Intel (after mediocre earnings reports from Alphabet and ServiceNow the previous day) sparked widespread investor anxiety regarding aggressive artificial intelligence spending and sustained cash burn.

As reported by CNBC, disappointing quarterly reports from both companies triggered a broad slide across technology equities and hardware suppliers, overshadowing positive momentum in other areas of the market. Investors grew increasingly wary of the sector's rising capital expenditures—the funds poured into long-term assets such as data centers and computing hardware.

With both firms spending heavily to build out artificial intelligence infrastructure, market participants are questioning when these massive investments will translate into meaningful revenue and profit growth per CNBC. The steep drops in Amazon and Intel weighed heavily on market indices, showing how vulnerabilities among dominant technology leaders can rapidly dampen confidence across the broader industry.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Cloudflare Slips Before Q3 After Facing Millions of PHP Exploit Attempts ©Изображения пользователя Maximusnd Zahar and Natali_Mis from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Cloudflare shares fell 2.7% to $310 on Thursday ahead of its November 5 report, after gaining about 46% over six months.

The company guided third-quarter revenue to $736 million to $737 million, up 31%, with adjusted EPS of $0.34.

At 34x forward sales and 210x forward earnings, the stock leaves little room for a miss, and adjusted gross margin fell to 73.1% last quarter.

Watch whether net retention holds near 120% and whether management raises full-year revenue guidance of $2.864 billion to $2.870 billion.

Last week, a cluster of PHP flaws knocked government websites offline and set off a global patching scramble. Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) saw millions of exploit attempts after the disclosure.

Events like this are why customers pay Cloudflare. The stock still slipped 2.7% to $310 on Thursday.

Shares are up about 46% over the past six months but sit 16% below their 52-week high of $370. The real test comes November 5, when Cloudflare reports third-quarter results.

The bar for November 5

Cloudflare raised the bar itself in August. Second-quarter revenue rose 36% to $696.1 million, topping consensus by about $30 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.29 beat by two cents.

For the third quarter, management guided to:

Revenue of $736 million to $737 million, up 31%

Adjusted operating income of $129 million to $130 million

Adjusted EPS of $0.34

It also raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.864 billion to $2.870 billion. Management has said it guides carefully because more deals now run on consumption and pool-of-funds contracts, which are harder to forecast.

Here's the trend heading into the print…

Cloudflare (NET): total revenue, quarterly, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, Q1 2025–Q4 2026 (TIKR)

Growth would cool to 31% if Cloudflare lands on its guide. A beat like the second quarter's would keep it in the mid 30s.

Machines are becoming the customer

CEO Matthew Prince framed the opportunity boldly in the second-quarter release. AI answer engines and agent-driven commerce are driving "a fundamental rewrite of the Internet for machine-to-machine traffic," he said.

The customer data backs him up. Cloudflare's developer base topped 10 million, up from 7.4 million a quarter earlier. Large customers rose 27% to 4,698 and now drive 73% of revenue.

Existing customers are spending more too. Dollar-based net retention climbed to 120%, up six points from a year ago, and current remaining performance obligations grew 35%.

Now compare that with the older incumbent…

Cloudflare (NET): total revenue vs Akamai (AKAM), $ billions, fiscal 2021–2025 (TIKR)

Akamai (AKAM:NASDAQ) grew second-quarter revenue just 5% to $1.1 billion. Its cloud infrastructure unit grew 39%, but on only $99 million of revenue, so Cloudflare is closing the size gap fast.

TIKR tracks 34 analysts on Cloudflare. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Cloudflare, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Cloudflare's Analyst Ratings

Paying up for the story

This is where it gets hard. Cloudflare trades at 34x forward sales and 210x forward earnings, and the average price target of $343 sits only about 11% above the current price.

What has that premium looked like over time?

Cloudflare (NET): forward (NTM) EV/Sales, last 3 years (TIKR)

Margins are also moving the wrong way. Adjusted gross margin fell to 73.1% in the second quarter from 76.3% a year earlier, and rising compute costs remain a risk. The GAAP operating loss reached $205.7 million after $151 million of restructuring charges.

Dilution is another overhang. Cloudflare sold $2.175 billion of 0% convertible notes due 2031 in August. Co-founder Michelle Zatlyn also sold about $27.5 million of stock in early October.

My take: Cloudflare is executing about as well as any software company right now, and the machine traffic story looks real to me. Yet at 34x sales, even a solid beat may not lift the stock much. I'd wait for a pullback before buying.

The checkpoint is November 5. A full-year guide raise and net retention holding near 120% would justify the multiple for another quarter.

title: Why Did Cloudflare Stock Jump?
detail:
Why Did Cloudflare Stock Jump?
Trefis Team

Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Shares of Cloudflare (NET) climbed 79.7% from January 31 to October 28, 2026, outpacing the 12.5% return of the S&P 500. The advance spanned three quarterly reports, ending with the most recent on August 6. The path was uneven: shares fell 23.6% on May 8, after the first-quarter report came with a 20% staff cut, and rose 10.5% on September 9 on a security partnership with OpenAI. The current share price appears to assume that developers and AI companies will sustain fast enough sales growth for the company to reach a reported profit. So are Cloudflare's sales really growing faster?

Cloudflare's Sales Are Growing Faster Than A Year Ago

So far, yes. Cloudflare generated $696 million in sales during the second quarter of fiscal 2026, reported on August 6. Revenue grew 35.9% in the quarter, compared with a 27.8% pace in the same period a year earlier.

The company is also securing larger contracts. Cloudflare announced in its February 10 report that it closed its largest deal on record by annual contract value, averaging $42.5 million a year. By the August 6 call, the number of customers paying more than $100,000 a year climbed 27% from a year earlier.

Management credits rapid growth in its Workers developer platform in particular. The company's own outlook is slower, however. Cloudflare guided to third-quarter revenue growth of 31%, with management stating they set guidance prudently as a shift toward pool-of-funds and consumption-based deals makes each quarter harder to forecast.

How Far Has Cloudflare's Operating Loss Narrowed?

Over the twelve months ending in June 2026, Cloudflare posted an operating loss equal to 8.1% of revenue. That margin narrowed from 9.9% a year earlier and 11.6% two years earlier.

The company's net loss widened to $170 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, up from $50.4 million a year earlier. Management reported $151 million in severance and other restructuring charges for the quarter. The filings data records those charges below the operating line, so the 8.1% operating loss above leaves them out. Without those expenses, executives said the net loss would have been roughly $18 million.

During the August 6 call, management said Cloudflare is pacing ahead of its goal to reach a GAAP profit by the end of 2028 at the latest. That is a target, not a result.

What Are You Paying For Cloudflare's Sales Now?

At the October 28 close, investors paid 45.0 times Cloudflare's sales over the past twelve months, compared with 3.2 times for the S&P 500. Based on those same twelve months of sales, the multiple was 34.6 at the end of June. The valuation climb since then has come from a higher price on revenue Cloudflare had already reported.

title: 5 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy: Picked By Hedge Funds
detail:
5 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy: Picked By Hedge Funds
Sanmit Amin
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:50 PM CDT 9 min read

Previously we covered the 10 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy According to Analysts. In this article we are going to take a look at hedge funds' top cybersecurity stock picks. Hedge funds are highly sensitive to valuation multiples. When high-growth cloud security stocks reach "nosebleed" price-to-sales multiples, hedge funds often take profits and rotate into diversified giants or enterprise consolidators. That's why we are expecting to see a different picture in this analysis.

Artificial intelligence is creating a bigger market for cybersecurity companies, but not for the reason investors might expect. The technology is helping defenders find weaknesses faster, while giving attackers new ways to exploit them. That leaves businesses facing a growing security challenge just as they begin integrating AI into more of their operations.

The problem has become increasingly visible. On October 23, Reuters reported that AI had contributed to a doubling of the number of digital vulnerabilities discovered year over year, according to research from cybersecurity firm VulnCheck. Recent flaws in widely used software also triggered disruptions, with some website operators temporarily taking their services offline rather than risk exploitation. Security experts warned that AI could shorten the time between discovering a vulnerability and developing a way to exploit it. The extent to which this will translate into successful attacks remains uncertain, but companies have less room to ignore weaknesses in their systems.

Businesses appear to be taking the risk seriously. PwC's October 2026 Global Digital Trust Insights survey found that 84% of security and finance leaders expect their cybersecurity budgets to increase over the next 12 months, up from 78% a year earlier. AI is also becoming a direct spending priority: 58% of security leaders ranked it among their top cybersecurity budget priorities. Yet half of the security leaders surveyed said attacks targeting AI systems were among the threats their organizations were least prepared to handle. That gap between investment and preparedness gives cybersecurity providers a practical opportunity to address a problem businesses are still struggling to solve.

The opportunity extends beyond protecting companies from AI-powered attacks. As businesses deploy AI agents and connect them to internal systems, they need stronger controls over identities, permissions and access to sensitive data. They also need tools that can detect suspicious activity and respond quickly, ideally without overwhelming already stretched security teams. Cybersecurity companies that can automate more of this work may be well positioned to benefit.

So, what are the best cybersecurity stocks? You can find the expanded list of 10 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy according to hedge funds here. We discussed the top 5 stocks below.

5 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy: Picked By Hedge Funds
Our Methodology

For this list, we looked at cybersecurity stocks that saw an increase in hedge fund ownership in Q2 2026 compared with the previous quarter, based on Insider Monkey's database. We then ranked the stocks by the number of hedge funds holding them at the end of Q2, from highest to lowest. When two stocks had the same number of hedge fund holders, we ranked the company with increased hedge fund interest in Q2 higher.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 599.2% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 372 percentage points (see more details here).

These strategy returns are measured through June 2, 2026.

5. Okta, Inc. (NASDAQ:OKTA)

Number of Hedge funds: 58

Market cap: $39.52 billion

Okta's opportunity comes down to identity. Businesses need to know who is accessing their systems, what that user is allowed to do and how to control access as they adopt AI agents. Okta's identity platform helps manage those permissions across applications and users, giving it a role as companies work out how to use AI without opening new security gaps.

Analysts generally like this position, and several raised their price targets in September and October. The latest results also showed solid profitability and cash generation. Revenue in Q2 fiscal 2027 rose 11% year over year to $805 million, subscription revenue grew 12%, and remaining performance obligations increased 17%. Free cash flow reached $227 million.

The question is whether Okta can accelerate from its current growth rate. Its identity products are well placed for an AI-heavy future, but the stock has rallied enough that investors need to see continued execution. Competition is another concern, as large cloud and security companies offer identity features of their own.

The number of hedge funds holding OKTA in Insider Monkey's database increased from 49 in Q1 to 58 in Q2 2026. Their combined stake value rose from $1.30 billion to $1.77 billion.

4. Fortinet, Inc. (NASDAQ:FTNT)

Number of Hedge funds: 62

Market cap: $135.74 billion

Fortinet's combination of networking and cybersecurity gives it a different route into the AI opportunity. Its firewalls and secure networking products protect data as it moves between users, applications and cloud environments. The company also develops hardware designed for security workloads, which can help customers manage performance as networks carry more traffic.

Fortinet had a strong Q2 2026, with revenue up 26% year over year to $2.05 billion. Product revenue jumped 52%, while billings grew 33%, prompting the company to raise its full-year revenue forecast. Analysts see plenty to like in the business, particularly the demand for its integrated security platform. Still, some have become more cautious about the stock after its strong rally. The concern is not so much about Fortinet's business, but how much of that growth investors have already priced in.

Fortinet looks well positioned to benefit from rising demand for cybersecurity, but a strong business does not automatically make a stock a good buy at any price. Investors will need to see the company keep delivering if its valuation is to be justified.

The number of hedge funds holding FTNT increased from 52 in Q1 to 62 in Q2 2026. The combined value of their stakes rose from $2.98 billion to $6.24 billion.

3. Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE:NET)

Number of Hedge funds: 87

Market cap: $116.72 billion

Cloudflare sits at the intersection of cybersecurity and the infrastructure needed to run AI applications. Its global network helps customers secure websites and applications, filter malicious traffic and improve performance. As the internet handles more machine-to-machine traffic from AI agents, Cloudflare could benefit from demand for both security and connectivity.

That opportunity has kept analysts broadly positive. Several analysts raised their price targets in October, citing Cloudflare's growth prospects and its role in the changing internet landscape.

The company's Q2 2026 revenue rose 36% year over year to $696.1 million, while current remaining performance obligations grew 35%. Those figures suggest demand remains strong, although Cloudflare is still reporting a GAAP operating loss.

The main concern is how much investors are paying for that growth. The stock is trading at 168x its forward earnings, although one needs to take that with a grain of salt, as razor-thin margin expectations have bloated the valuation. That said, the company is yet to prove that it can expand its margins.

The AI opportunity is real, but investors should not assume Cloudflare will capture all the value created by AI-driven internet traffic.

The number of hedge funds holding NET in Insider Monkey's database increased from 84 in Q1 to 87 in Q2 2026. Their combined stake value rose from $3.55 billion to $3.98 billion.

2. Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ:PANW)

Number of Hedge funds: 89

Market cap: $328.59 billion

Palo Alto Networks combines a broad security platform with strong growth in its newer products. The company covers network security, cloud security and security operations, helping customers consolidate tools across a complex mix of systems. That strategy is particularly relevant as businesses add AI applications and look for a single platform to manage more of their security needs.

Analysts remain broadly positive, and several raised their price targets. Their main argument is that Palo Alto can keep expanding its newer security businesses while benefiting from companies that want fewer vendors and better integration. Its fiscal Q4 2026 revenue grew 34% year over year to $3.41 billion, while next-generation security annual recurring revenue jumped 63% to $9.10 billion.

The valuation is the main drawback. Palo Alto's forward P/E of 93x already reflects high expectations, and the average analyst price target is close to its current share price. Strong results may therefore be needed just to sustain the stock's premium.

The number of hedge funds holding PANW in Insider Monkey's database increased from 87 in Q1 to 89 in Q2 2026. Their combined stake value rose sharply from $2.12 billion to $5.49 billion.

1. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWD)

Number of Hedge funds: 89

Market cap: $275.02 billion

CrowdStrike has become one of the leading names in cybersecurity by bringing endpoint protection, cloud security and other tools together on its Falcon platform. Customers can add more protection without assembling a separate product for every threat, which helps CrowdStrike expand its relationship with existing accounts.

Analysts remain broadly bullish, and several raised their price targets in recent weeks. The key support for that view is the company's recurring revenue growth and growing adoption of its broader platform. In Q2 fiscal 2027, CrowdStrike generated record net new annual recurring revenue of $333 million, up 51% year over year. Its Falcon Flex business also saw annual recurring revenue grow 101% to $2.29 billion, while free cash flow reached $377 million.

CrowdStrike still has plenty going for it, but its high valuation means there's not much room for a slowdown. It needs to keep bringing in new customers and getting existing ones to spend more, all while competing with Palo Alto Networks and other deep-pocketed rivals. Its broad platform gives it room to grow, but the company has to deliver on those expectations.

Hedge fund interest in the stock also picked up. Insider Monkey's database showed that 89 hedge funds held CrowdStrike at the end of Q2 2026, up from 79 in Q1. The combined value of their reported stakes climbed from $2.52 billion to $4.54 billion.

While CRWD is the most popular cybersecurity stock among hedge funds, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than CRWD that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock.

F5 (FFIV) stock fell 20.4% on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, while the S&P 500 rose 0.3%. The decline came the day after the company's October 27 release of results for its fiscal fourth quarter of 2026, which topped analysts' estimates for both adjusted earnings per share and revenue. The beat was only part of the release, as F5 also issued its outlook for the new fiscal year. So what exactly did F5 report, and what does it expect for fiscal 2027?

F5 Beat Estimates But Expects Slower Revenue Growth

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, F5 posted adjusted earnings per share of $4.42, beating the $4.26 estimate. Revenue reached $917.4 million, exceeding the projected $884.0 million. Management said the 13% revenue growth from a year earlier surpassed the top of its own guidance range. Product revenue climbed 23%, while services revenue increased 3%.

For fiscal 2027, management guided to total revenue growth of 8% to 9%, below the 11% F5 reported for fiscal 2026. Not every part of the business is expected to slow. Management expects software to grow at a solid double-digit rate, after 8% growth in fiscal 2026. It expects growth in systems to be stronger in the first half of the year than in the second, and tied the slower second half to the cyclical part of an ongoing systems refresh.

Management also said its fiscal 2027 gross margin outlook reflects higher component costs, projecting an adjusted gross margin of 80.5% to 82.5% for the year. Fourth-quarter cash flow reflected inventory builds and supplier prepayments made to secure supply for fiscal 2027 revenue, management said, and F5 expects to keep increasing inventory in fiscal 2027. Operating cash flow in the fourth quarter was $118 million, compared with $208 million a year earlier.

Did Companies Like F5 Fall Too?

They did, but by far less. All five companies on F5's Trefis peer list fell during the same session. Fortinet recorded the largest decline of the five, dropping 5.9%, while Cisco Systems, another company on the list, lost 1.0%. The wider technology sector went the other way, as XLK, the SPDR fund for the sector, gained 0.8%. F5's drop was more than three times the size of Fortinet's, so the stock moved largely on its own rather than with its group.

Where Does F5 Stock Stand After The Fall?

F5 had not fallen this much in a single session at any time in the prior 365 days.

Over the twelve months to October 28, F5 stock returned 25.9%, compared with 14.0% for the S&P 500. The shares closed at a 52-week high of $479.83 on October 9, 2026, up from a 52-week low of $223.99 on November 19, 2025. After the drop they ended Wednesday at $365.53, about 24% below that high. Over the month to October 28, a period that includes the drop, the stock lost 16.6%, while the S&P 500 gained 1.0%.

What F5 Reported, and What It Promised

Revenue came in at $917.43 million, up 13%, against a $885.10 million consensus. Non-GAAP EPS of $4.42 exceeded the $4.26 estimate. It was F5's ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit product revenue growth.

The guidance was the problem. F5 guided first-quarter non-GAAP EPS to $4.25 to $4.37, and consensus is at $4.36, near the top of that range. For fiscal 2027, F5 guided revenue growth of 8% to 9% and EPS of $18.00 to $18.30.

CFO Cooper Werner said on the call that gross margin will reflect "the higher component costs we have discussed previously" and that "the biggest driver on OpEx is investments that we are making to drive future growth." The board signed off on a new $1.5 billion buyback authorization. Keep in mind that an authorization gives F5 permission to buy back stock and does not require it. Doubling AI security specialist sellers in 2027 is a stated plan that has yet to be delivered.

Read-Through for Both Stocks

F5: The core issue is the hardware refresh cycle (customers replacing aging equipment). Werner said replacement revenue "is going to decline over the back half of the year." Direct AI bookings were well over $100 million, which is still small next to $3.42 billion in annual revenue.

Fortinet: Revenue rose 20% and billings climbed 29%. The stock still trades at about 69 times earnings, a multiple that only works if results keep getting better every quarter.

FTNT Earnings Explorer — 24/7 Wall St.
Hidden Price Hikes Behind the Growth

Part of the growth at both companies comes from higher prices. Fortinet's CEO Ken Xie said pricing had about a 10% impact on billings growth, and he called prices "stabilized, but not improved yet." F5 is stockpiling components ahead of a tight memory market. Reuters described the selloff as software stocks failing to meet lofty investor expectations. F5 did not put a dollar figure on AI security revenue for 2027, and it gave no number for product growth beyond calling it double-digit.

Cloudflare (NYSE:NET) is my second-largest position, so I've followed application security stocks for years. In my experience, when the market punishes good results like this, it's usually reacting to the stock price rather than the business.

Was the F5 Selloff Overdone?

Mostly no. It was a fair repricing. At $364.96, F5 trades at about 20 times its guided fiscal 2027 EPS. That's a reasonable price for a company growing in the high single digits, and the cheap price was the part that went away. If you believe AI security will offset the fading refresh cycle, this level looks fair. If you think the refresh cycle was carrying the growth, there is less room to rebound.

Here is the test you can check: the fiscal first quarter, which ends December 31, 2026. If F5 reports non-GAAP EPS above $4.37 and keeps the 8% to 9% revenue outlook, the drop went too far. A result below $4.36 would show the market was right to sell on a lukewarm outlook after an 80% year.
